title: Test suite for semantic search upgrade
description:
## Objective

Add comprehensive unit and integration tests covering all new functionality from the semantic search upgrade: config parsing, prompt template application (including edge cases), fingerprint changes, reranker JSON parsing, reranker fallback behavior, metrics calculation, stale index diagnostics, backward compatibility with pre-upgrade configs, metrics concurrency safety, and mocked HTTP server integration tests — while preserving all existing test coverage.

## Behavior under test

- Config parsing with and without rerank block.
- Config parsing with and without prompt templates.
- Config parsing: completely pre-upgrade config file (no semantic-search section at all) parses correctly.
- Query prompt template application to input text.
- Document prompt template application to input text.
- Template edge cases: empty string, whitespace-only, special characters (newlines, unicode), template containing both {query} and {text}.
- Template validation (unknown placeholders, empty templates).
- Semantic fingerprint change when document prompt changes.
- No fingerprint change when only query prompt changes.
- Reranker JSON parsing (bare array, markdown-fenced, unknown IDs, missing IDs).
- Reranker fallback behavior (timeout, HTTP error, parse failure).
- Metrics summary calculation: min/median/max/mean.
- Zero-result diagnostics emission.
- Low-score diagnostics emission.
- Stale index diagnostics emission.
- Concurrent access safety for rolling aggregates (if thread-safe metrics are implemented).
- Integration: OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint receives prompted query.
- Integration: OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint receives prompted document chunks.
- Integration: Reranker endpoint receives candidate list and returns reordered IDs.
- Integration: Reranker failure falls back to original result order.

## Test layer

- Unit tests for config parsing, template application, fingerprint, metrics, diagnostics.
- Integration tests with mocked HTTP servers for backend interaction.

## Source references

- Primary planning artifact: `docs/semantic-search-upgrade-20260524.md` §7 "Add tests"
- Spec sections: §7 (all test requirements, unit and integration test lists)

## Current test state

- Existing semantic search tests exist for current config parsing and search behavior.
- No tests exist for prompt templates, reranking, metrics, or the enhanced response format.

## Desired test state

- All spec scenarios from §7 covered by unit or integration tests.
- All review-recommended edge cases covered (empty/whitespace templates, backward compat, stale index, concurrency).
- All existing tests continue to pass.
- New tests follow existing test patterns in the codebase.

## Scope

In scope:
- Unit tests: config parsing with/without rerank block.
- Unit tests: config parsing with pre-upgrade config (no semantic-search section at all).
- Unit tests: query/document prompt application (normal case).
- Unit tests: template edge cases (empty, whitespace-only, special chars, both placeholders).
- Unit tests: template validation (unknown placeholders, missing placeholders).
- Unit tests: semantic fingerprint change logic.
- Unit tests: reranker JSON parser (bare array, markdown fences, unknown IDs, missing IDs).
- Unit tests: reranker fallback logic.
- Unit tests: metrics calculation (min/median/max/mean).
- Unit tests: metrics concurrent access safety (if thread-safe metrics implemented).
- Unit tests: diagnostics (zero-result, low-score, stale-index).
- Integration tests: mocked HTTP for embedding with prompts.
- Integration tests: mocked HTTP for reranker interaction and fallback.

Out of scope:
- End-to-end tests requiring real LLM endpoints.
- Performance/benchmark tests.
- Tests for features not part of this upgrade.

## Pre-condition: Mock HTTP infrastructure investigation

BEFORE starting integration test implementation:
1. Investigate whether the project already has mock HTTP test utilities (wiremock, mockito, custom tokio-based test server, etc.).
2. If a mock HTTP pattern exists, adopt it.
3. If none exists, implement a simple HTTP test helper (tokio-based mock server or wiremock crate) that all integration tests can use.
4. Document the mock HTTP pattern for future tests.

## Implementation plan

1. Inspect existing test patterns, fixtures, and mock infrastructure in the project.
2. [Pre-condition] Investigate mock HTTP infrastructure (see above).
3. Add unit tests alongside each new module:
   a. Config parsing tests (new fields, backward compat, edge cases).
   b. Template application tests (normal + edge cases).
   c. Fingerprint tests.
   d. Reranker JSON parser tests.
   e. Reranker fallback tests.
   f. Metrics calculation tests.
   g. Diagnostics tests (zero-result, low-score, stale-index).
   h. Thread-safe metrics concurrency test (if applicable).
4. Add integration tests for HTTP-backed backends using the project's existing or new HTTP test utilities.
5. Ensure all existing tests pass.
6. Run validation.

## Acceptance criteria

### Config parsing
- [ ] Missing rerank block → parses as disabled.
- [ ] Rerank block present → parses correctly.
- [ ] Pre-upgrade config (no semantic-search section) → parses correctly in legacy mode.

### Template application
- [ ] Query prompt template applied to query text correctly.
- [ ] Document prompt template applied to document text correctly.
- [ ] Empty template string: treated as unset (no template applied).
- [ ] Whitespace-only template string: treated as unset (no template applied).
- [ ] Template with special characters (newlines, unicode): applied correctly.
- [ ] Template with both {query} and {text}: context-appropriate placeholder used.
- [ ] Template validation: unknown placeholders handled gracefully (config parse error).
- [ ] Template validation: non-empty template with no recognized placeholder produces config parse error.

### Fingerprint
- [ ] Document prompt change → fingerprint changes.
- [ ] Only query prompt change → no fingerprint change.

### Reranker JSON parser
- [ ] Bare JSON array parsed correctly.
- [ ] Markdown-fenced JSON parsed correctly.
- [ ] Unknown candidate IDs silently ignored.
- [ ] Missing candidate IDs appended to end in original order.
- [ ] Partial/truncated JSON: parse what's available, append missing IDs, log warning.

### Reranker fallback
- [ ] On timeout/HTTP error/parse failure: returns original ordering.
- [ ] Strict mode: on failure, returns error instead of falling back.
- [ ] Zero candidates: no API call made.

### Metrics
- [ ] min/median/max/mean calculated correctly.
- [ ] Empty result list: min/max/median/mean are None (not crash).
- [ ] Concurrent access to rolling aggregates: safe and correct (if thread-safe metrics implemented).

### Diagnostics
- [ ] Zero results emits warning.
- [ ] Low score emits warning.
- [ ] Stale index emits warning.
- [ ] Warning cooldown: same warning not re-emitted within cooldown interval.

### Integration (mocked HTTP)
- [ ] Embedding receives prompted query text.
- [ ] Embedding receives prompted document chunks.
- [ ] Reranker receives candidate list and reorders.
- [ ] Reranker failure falls back to original ordering.
- [ ] Reranker strict mode: failure returns error response.

### Non-regression
- [ ] All existing tests still pass.
- [ ] `cargo test` — all tests pass.
- [ ] `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.

## Validation commands

- `cargo test` — all tests pass.
- `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: Features 1, 2, and 3 (tests are written against the actual implementation).

## Review requirements

- User PR review required.

## Handoff requirements

- Files changed: test files alongside new modules + test helpers.
- Validation evidence: test output.
- Discovered Beads: none expected.
- Spec updates if behavior changed: spec is the primary artifact.

title: Search pipeline metrics and response diagnostics
description:
## Objective

Add lightweight per-query and aggregate metrics collection around AFT's semantic search pipeline so users and tools can understand search quality, diagnose misconfiguration, and monitor performance — without leaking query content or code snippets.

## Current behavior

- `aft_search` returns ranked results with scores but no pipeline diagnostics.
- No timing, score distribution, candidate count, or pipeline metadata.
- No aggregate metrics or warning heuristics.

## Desired behavior

- Per-query metrics collected for every semantic/hybrid search call.
- `aft_search` response includes optional `diagnostics` metadata object.
- Human-readable output includes a compact one-line footer.
- Rolling aggregate metrics maintained in memory over a configurable window (default: last 100 queries) — p50/p95/p99 latency, reranker failure rate, etc.
- Configurable warning thresholds (with cooldown/deadband to prevent noise) emit diagnostics when retrieval quality is poor.
- Metrics collection is thread-safe — the data structures use atomic counters or guarded access so concurrent queries (should the pipeline become multi-threaded) do not race.
- No raw query text or code snippets in logs unless verbose debug mode is explicitly enabled.

## Scope

In scope:
- Define `SearchDiagnostics` struct with fields from spec §4: latency breakdown per pipeline stage (embedding, lexical, semantic retrieval, hybrid fusion, reranking), candidate counts per stage, score distribution (min/median/max/mean), warning flags.
- Define `SearchMetrics` struct with rolling aggregate counters: p50/p95/p99 latency, reranker failure count/rate, total queries, diagnostic summaries.
- Instrument existing semantic and hybrid search paths with timing and count collection.
- Add optional `diagnostics` field to `aft_search` response, gated by config flag or always-present.
- Add compact human-readable footer line.
- Implement rolling aggregate statistics (configurable window size, default 100 queries).
- Add warning threshold config, cooldown/deadband (same warning type not re-emitted within configurable interval, default: 60s), and diagnostics emission.
- Ensure query text and code snippets are NOT logged by default (hash-only for queries).
- Metrics struct designed for thread safety: use atomic counters where applicable; metrics module does not assume single-threaded access.
- For stages that run in parallel (e.g., lexical + semantic in hybrid search), total latency = max(stage latencies), not sum. Each stage reports its own wall-clock duration.
- On semantic config change (reconfigure/restart), rolling aggregates are reset. In-flight query metrics complete but are excluded from the new aggregate window.

Out of scope:
- TUI integration (separate bead).
- Reranking instrumentation (covered by Feature 2 + this bead's integration).
- Alerting or external monitoring export.
- Persistent metrics storage across AFT restarts.
- Documentation (separate bead).

## Mandatory code/spec reading before editing

- [ ] `crates/aft/src/commands/` — `aft_search` response type and handler.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — existing semantic search pipeline to find instrumentation points.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — config structs for adding warning threshold fields.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — existing JSON serialization patterns for response types.
- [ ] `docs/semantic-search-upgrade-20260524.md` §4 — exact diagnostics schema fields.

## Implementation plan

1. Define `SearchDiagnostics` struct with all fields from spec §4.
2. Define `SearchMetrics` struct with rolling aggregate counters (configurable window, default 100; thread-safe design with atomics).
3. Add `semantic_diagnostics: bool` config flag (default: false, implicit true when diagnostics requested).
4. Instrument embedding call with timing.
5. Instrument lexical search with timing (if applicable).
6. Instrument semantic retrieval and hybrid fusion with timing.
7. Instrument reranking with timing (when enabled). For parallel stages, report max latency, not sum.
8. Collect score statistics (min/median/max/mean) from results.
9. Collect candidate counts at each pipeline stage.
10. Add optional `diagnostics` field to `aft_search` response struct.
11. Add human-readable footer line to text output.
12. Implement rolling aggregate metrics over a ring buffer with configurable capacity.
13. Add warning threshold config with cooldown (no duplicate warnings within cooldown period, default 60s).
14. Ensure query privacy: hash query string for metrics, not raw text.
15. Define reset behavior on config change: rolling aggregates cleared, in-flight query snapshots excluded.
16. Add tests.
17. Run validation.

## Error handling and edge cases

- No semantic search config: diagnostics should be empty/null, not error.
- Zero results: score statistics should handle empty list gracefully (None for min/max/median/mean).
- Pipeline stages that don't run (e.g., lexical disabled): latency = 0, candidate_count = 0.
- Metrics overflow: use sane max values/capping.
- Rolling aggregates: reset on config change. Window parameter configurable (default 100).
- Query hash collisions: document as possible but acceptably rare.
- Warning cooldown: same warning type not re-emitted within cooldown interval (default 60s) to prevent noise on repeated poor-quality results.
- Concurrent access: metrics struct uses atomic counters for non-sequential counters; rolling aggregator uses a Mutex or RwLock for the window buffer. Not in hot path — lock contention negligible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `aft_search` response includes optional `diagnostics` object when semantic search is configured.
- [ ] Human-readable output includes a compact one-line footer with key metrics.
- [ ] Per-query latency breakdowns are collected for each pipeline stage.
- [ ] Score distribution (min/median/max/mean) is computed from results.
- [ ] Candidate counts are tracked per stage.
- [ ] Rolling p50/p95/p99 latency is maintained over a configurable window (default 100 queries).
- [ ] For parallel pipeline stages, total latency = max of stage latencies, not sum.
- [ ] Warning thresholds emit diagnostics for zero results, low scores, stale index.
- [ ] Warning cooldown: same warning type not re-emitted within cooldown interval (default 60s).
- [ ] Warnings say "pipeline may be misconfigured" not "model is bad".
- [ ] Query text is never logged; only query string hash is stored unless debug mode is on.
- [ ] Metrics collection is thread-safe (atomics + guarded ring buffer, not racy).
- [ ] On config change, rolling aggregates are reset cleanly.
- [ ] Existing `aft_search` response format is not broken (diagnostics is additive).
- [ ] All existing tests pass unchanged.

## Validation commands

- `cargo build` — compiles.
- `cargo test` — all tests pass.
- `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.

## Dependencies

- Blocks: Story 4 (TUI integration consumes metrics/diagnostics), Task 5 (docs), Task 6 (test coverage).
- Integration point with Feature 2: reads reranking per-query timing from the pipeline — coordinate on the exact struct shape.

## Review requirements

- User PR review required.
- Privacy review: verify no raw queries/code in logs by default.

## Handoff requirements

- Files changed: new metrics/diagnostics module, search pipeline instrumentation, response types.
- Validation evidence: test output.
- Discovered Beads: none expected.
- Spec updates if behavior changed: spec is the primary artifact.

title: OpenAI-compatible reranking pipeline
description:
## Objective

Add an optional reranking stage to AFT's semantic search pipeline. When configured, overfetch N candidates from the first-stage retrieval, split them into windows, send each window to an OpenAI-compatible chat/completions endpoint with a deterministic listwise reranking prompt, parse the returned JSON (bare array or markdown-fenced, ignoring unknown IDs and appending missing ones), and return the reordered top-K results. On any failure (timeout, HTTP error, parse failure), fall back to original first-stage ordering with a logged WARN-level message — unless strict mode is configured, in which case the search fails with an error.

## Current behavior

- Semantic search returns top-K candidates from embedding similarity only.
- No reordering, no contextual reranking.
- No support for cross-encoder or LLM-based reranking.

## Desired behavior

- New optional `rerank` config block on the semantic search config (disabled by default).
- When `rerank` is enabled: overfetch candidates, rerank via LLM, return reordered top-K.
- Compatible with any OpenAI-compatible chat/completions backend (base_url, model, api_key, max_retries, timeout).
- Configurable window size: candidates reranked in batches (default: 20; must account for model context window minus prompt overhead).
- Configurable overfetch factor: how many extra candidates to retrieve (default: 3x top-K).
- Deterministic listwise reranking prompt (temperature=0, seed if supported).
- Strict mode (default: off): when enabled, reranker failure causes the search to return an error response instead of silently falling back.
- SSRF validation on reranker base_url, shared with the embedding backend validation via a utility function.
- Per-query reranking metadata available for diagnostics (covered by Feature 3 integration).
- When reranker is disabled or fails: existing semantic search behavior unmodified.

## Scope

In scope:
- Define `RerankConfig` struct with all fields (base_url, model, api_key, window_size, overfetch_factor, strict_mode, max_retries, timeout_secs).
- Implement `Reranker` trait or module that wraps the OpenAI-compatible chat/completions call.
- Implement windowed listwise reranking logic with deterministic prompt.
- Implement JSON response parser supporting bare array, markdown-fenced, unknown IDs (silently dropped), missing IDs (appended to end in original order).
- Integrate reranking step into the semantic search pipeline (after first-stage retrieval, before top-K selection).
- Implement fallback-on-failure with WARN-level log message (via AFT's env_logger).
- Implement strict mode: on failure, search returns an error code rather than falling back.
- Extract SSRF URL validation to a shared utility function (`crates/aft/src/`) used by both the embedding and reranker backends — no copy-paste.
- Ensure query privacy: the reranker prompt includes only candidate IDs and optionally the code snippet, no raw query text unless explicitly configured.
- Config deserialization backward compatibility (missing rerank block = disabled).

Out of scope:
- Non-OpenAI-compatible reranker backends (cross-encoders, Cohere Rerank, BGE-reranker).
- Reranker prompt customization (hardcoded for MVP).
- Caching of rerank results across identical queries.
- TUI changes (separate bead).
- Metrics/diagnostics (separate bead, integration point noted).

## Mandatory code/spec reading before editing

- [ ] `crates/aft/src/commands/` — existing `aft_search` pipeline to find integration point.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — existing OpenAI-compatible embedding backend for pattern reference (SSRF validation, client construction).
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — config structs for semantic search to add the rerank block.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — existing JSON serialization patterns for response types.

## Implementation plan

1. Read existing semantic search pipeline to identify where reranking fits.
2. Read existing OpenAI-compatible client code for pattern reuse.
3. Read existing SSRF validation to extract to shared utility.
4. Define `RerankConfig` struct.
5. Extract shared SSRF validation utility function.
6. Implement JSON response parser (bare array, markdown-fenced, unknown IDs, missing IDs).
7. Implement `rerank_candidates(candidates, query, config) -> Result<Vec<ScoredCandidate>>` function.
8. Write listwise reranking prompt.
9. Wire reranking call into search pipeline with overfetch → rerank → top-K flow.
10. Add fallback behavior with WARN logging on failure.
11. Add strict mode behavior (error on failure).
12. Update response metadata.
13. Add unit and integration tests.
14. Run validation.

## Error handling and edge cases

- Timeout or HTTP error from reranker: fallback to original ordering (or error in strict mode), logged at WARN level via AFT's standard env_logger.
- Non-JSON response: same fallback behavior.
- Valid JSON but unexpected structure (e.g., array of objects instead of array of numbers): same fallback.
- Partial JSON (e.g., truncated array): parse what's available, append missing IDs in original order, log partial parse at WARN level.
- LLM returns reordered set that is a permutation of the input (issue #1: unknown IDs dropped; issue #2: missing IDs appended).
- Prompt injection: candidates whose code excerpts contain instruction-overriding text are handled at the protocol level (candidate content delimited clearly in prompt). Document that the upstream LLM's own safety behavior is outside AFT's control.
- Window sizing: each window must fit within the model's context limit minus prompt tokens. Sane default: 20 candidates. Document the issue for users with large snippets or small-context models.
- No candidates returned from first stage: skip reranking entirely, return empty results.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Config with no rerank block: search behavior unchanged, no reranking applied.
- [ ] Config with rerank block: overfetches candidates from first-stage retrieval.
- [ ] Config with rerank block: sends each window to the configured endpoint.
- [ ] Config with rerank block: returns reordered top-K results when LLM responds correctly.
- [ ] Invalid JSON response from reranker: fallback to original ordering, WARN-level log message (env_logger).
- [ ] Timeout/HTTP error from reranker: fallback to original ordering, WARN-level log message (env_logger).
- [ ] Unknown candidate IDs in reranker response: silently ignored.
- [ ] Missing candidate IDs (fewer IDs than expected): appended to end in original order.
- [ ] Markdown-fenced JSON response: parsed correctly.
- [ ] Bare JSON array response: parsed correctly.
- [ ] SSRF validation applied to reranker base_url.
- [ ] SSRF validation uses the same shared utility as the embedding backend.
- [ ] Strict mode (enabled): reranker failure returns an error response (search fails).
- [ ] Strict mode (disabled, default): reranker failure falls back with WARN log.
- [ ] Configuration validation: rerank block enabled without base_url returns a config error.
- [ ] Configuration validation: rerank block enabled with invalid SSRF URL returns a config error.
- [ ] Zero first-stage candidates: reranking skipped, empty results returned, no API call made.
- [ ] API keys: not stored in config file or logged in clear text. Debug logging masks query params in URLs.
- [ ] All existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo build` and `cargo clippy` pass.

## Validation commands

- `cargo build` — compiles.
- `cargo test` — all tests pass.
- `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: none (independent code path, though prompt template config pattern from Feature 1 is advisory).
- Blocks: Feature 3 (reranking instrumentation), Story 4 (TUI status), Task 5 (docs), Task 6 (tests for reranker paths).

## Review requirements

- User PR review required.
- Security review: SSRF validation coverage and API key handling.

## Handoff requirements

- Files changed: new reranker module, search pipeline integration, config structs, shared SSRF validation.
- Validation evidence: test output.
- Discovered Beads: none expected.
- Spec updates if behavior changed: spec is the primary artifact.

title: Embedding prompt-template support
description:
## Objective

Add optional `query_prompt_template` and `document_prompt_template` string fields to AFT's semantic search config. When configured, these templates wrap raw query/document text before embedding — critical for instruction-tuned embedding models like OASIS-code-embedding that require a prefix like `"Instruct: Given a code search query, retrieve relevant code snippet that answer the query\nQuery: {query}"`. Other models (especially fastembed/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) should not receive such prefixes. We need an opt-in system: optional template fields on the semantic config, separate methods for embed_query vs embed_documents, and a fingerprint change when document templates change.

## Current behavior

- Single `embed` method per backend receives raw text with no prompt.
- No distinction between query embedding and document embedding.
- Semantic index fingerprint does not include any prompt-template identity.

## Desired behavior

- Backends expose `embed_query(text)` and `embed_documents(texts)` methods.
- `embed_query` applies query_prompt_template if configured.
- `embed_documents` applies document_prompt_template if configured.
- Template syntax: `{query}` or `{text}` placeholder replaced with raw input.
- Semantic index fingerprint includes a hash of the document_prompt_template value.
- query_prompt_template changes do not force index rebuild but are tracked in diagnostics.
- Default configs for all backends (fastembed, openai_compatible, ollama) leave both templates unset — zero behavior change by default.
- Startup warning emitted when prompt templates are configured for known non-instruction-tuned models (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2).

## Scope

In scope:
- Add `query_prompt_template: Option<String>` and `document_prompt_template: Option<String>` to semantic backend config.
- Refactor `EmbeddingBackend` trait to split `embed_query` and `embed_documents`.
- Add `apply_query_template(text) -> String` and `apply_document_template(text) -> String` helper methods.
- Update semantic index fingerprint computation to include document prompt template identity.
- Ensure all backends use the appropriate method in the right context.
- Config deserialization backward compatibility (missing fields = None).
- Update config validation to accept but not require these fields.
- Add startup warning when templates are configured for known non-instruction-tuned models.
- Empty or whitespace-only template strings normalized to None at deserialization time.

Out of scope:
- Reranking pipeline (separate bead).
- Search diagnostics/metrics (separate bead).
- TUI changes (separate bead).
- Documentation updates beyond inline code docs (separate bead).

## Mandatory code/spec reading before editing

- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — existing embedding backend trait and implementations.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — semantic index config and fingerprint computation.
- [ ] `crates/aft/src/` — existing semantic search pipeline where embed is called.
- [ ] Existing tests around embedding and config parsing.

## Implementation plan

1. Read existing `EmbeddingBackend` trait and all backend implementations (fastembed, openai_compatible, ollama).
2. Read semantic index config struct.
3. Read semantic index fingerprint computation.
4. Add template fields to config struct with `#[serde(default)]` / `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.
5. Refactor trait: keep `embed()` as the **required** method. Add `embed_query()` and `embed_documents()` as **provided methods with default implementations** that delegate to `embed()`. Backends that need template support override `embed_query()`/`embed_documents()` directly. This ensures no existing backend or test breaks — all existing impls continue implementing only `embed()`. Verify no cyclic delegation (embed → embed_query default → embed would be infinite).
6. Add `apply_query_template`/`apply_document_template` helpers on the config or a new helper struct. Validate templates at config parse time: if a recognized placeholder is present, apply the template; if neither `{query}` nor `{text}` is found and the template is non-empty, produce a config parse error.
7. Wire template application into each backend's embed_query/embed_documents.
8. Update fingerprint computation to hash document_prompt_template.
9. Update all call sites to use the correct method.
10. Add/update tests.
11. Run validation.

## Error handling and edge cases

- Missing/unset templates: pass raw text unchanged.
- Empty or whitespace-only template strings: normalize to None at deserialization time (not at query time). No template applied, no fingerprint change.
- `{query}` and `{text}` placeholders: if template contains both placeholders, context determines which is used (query context: `{query}`, document context: `{text}`). If neither recognized placeholder is found and template is non-empty, produce a config parse error at load time.
- Template with only one recognized placeholder (e.g., only `{query}` in a document template): still applied — the template is used regardless of context mismatch.
- Backward compat: configs without these fields deserialize to None.
- Fingerprint: None document_prompt_template always produces same hash regardless of absent vs explicit-None.
- Trait recursion guard: `embed_query()` default delegates to `embed()`; `embed()` must NOT call `embed_query()` back. The delegation is one-directional. Tests verify no stack overflow from cyclic defaults.
- Startup warning: AFT checks the configured model name against a known list of non-instruction-tuned models at startup. If templates are configured for a model in this list, emit a WARN-level log message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing configs deserialize successfully with new optional fields absent.
- [ ] Default config (no templates) produces raw query embeddings — no prompt applied.
- [ ] Config with query_prompt_template embeds the transformed query string.
- [ ] Config with document_prompt_template embeds transformed chunk text.
- [ ] document_prompt_template change alters semantic index fingerprint.
- [ ] query_prompt_template change does not alter semantic index fingerprint.
- [ ] All three backends (fastembed, openai_compatible, ollama) support templates.
- [ ] Empty or whitespace-only template string treated identically to None — no template applied, no fingerprint change.
- [ ] Invalid template (non-empty with no recognized placeholder) produces a config parse error.
- [ ] Template containing both `{query}` and `{text}` applies context-appropriate placeholder.
- [ ] Known non-instruction-tuned model with configured templates emits startup WARN-level log message.
- [ ] Trait has no cyclic delegation: existing backends implementing only `embed()` still compile and work.
- [ ] All existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] New tests cover the above acceptance criteria.
- [ ] `cargo build` and `cargo clippy` pass.

## Validation commands

- `cargo build` — compiles.
- `cargo test` — all tests pass.
- `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.

## Review requirements

- User PR review required.

## Handoff requirements

- Files changed: config struct, embedding trait + impls, fingerprint computation, call sites.
- Validation evidence: test output.
- Discovered Beads: none expected.
- Spec updates if behavior changed: spec is the primary artifact.

title: Semantic search upgrade: prompt-templates, reranking, diagnostics, TUI
description:
## Program goal

Upgrade AFT's semantic search from a single-pass embedding retrieval to a configurable two-stage pipeline with optional query/document prompt-templates, an OpenAI-compatible reranking stage, per-query and aggregate diagnostics, and TUI status integration — while preserving full backward compatibility with the existing default (fastembed/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) behavior.

## Source references

- Primary planning artifact: `docs/semantic-search-upgrade-20260524.md`
- Behavior/spec references: `docs/semantic-search-upgrade-20260524.md`
- Design references: AFT existing semantic search implementation under `crates/aft/src/`

## Context summary

AFT currently provides semantic search using cAST-style symbol chunking with fastembed, openai_compatible, and ollama embedding backends. The default is fastembed/all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Users who want better retrieval quality with instruction-tuned embedding models (like OASIS-code-embedding) currently have no way to configure query-side prompt templates. There is no reranking stage at all — users must accept first-stage retrieval order. Search diagnostics are minimal, making it hard to diagnose low-quality retrieval. The spec at `docs/semantic-search-upgrade-20260524.md` defines a comprehensive upgrade path addressing all these gaps.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Existing default AFT semantic search (fastembed/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) works identically before and after the upgrade — no regression.
- [ ] Users can configure query_prompt_template and document_prompt_template per embedding backend.
- [ ] document_prompt_template changes trigger a semantic index fingerprint change (forcing rebuild).
- [ ] query_prompt_template changes are tracked in diagnostics but do not force index rebuild.
- [ ] A new reranking pipeline can be enabled via config (default: disabled).
- [ ] Reranking uses an OpenAI-compatible chat/completions backend with configurable model, window_size, candidate_count, timeout, and temperature.
- [ ] Reranking failure falls back cleanly to first-stage ordering (unless strict mode is explicitly configured).
- [ ] Search pipeline records per-query and aggregate metrics (latency breakdowns, score distributions, candidate counts, backend/model info).
- [ ] `aft_search` response includes optional diagnostics metadata without breaking existing human-readable output.
- [ ] TUI/status panel shows semantic pipeline health (index status, backend/model, last query latency, score summary, rerank status).
- [ ] Tests cover config parsing, prompt template application, fingerprint changes, reranker JSON parsing, fallback behavior, metrics calculation, and integration with mocked HTTP servers.
- [ ] README/config docs updated with example configs for fastembed default, OASIS-only, and OASIS+CodeRankLLM setups.
- [ ] All child Beads complete.
- [ ] Verification Bead complete.

## Non-goals

- Support for Reranker backends other than OpenAI-compatible chat/completions (e.g., Cohere, cross-encoders) — future work.
- Non-OpenAI-compatible reranking APIs.
- Automatic prompt-template selection by model name — users must configure explicitly.
- Changing the default embedding backend or model.
- Breaking changes to `aft_search` response schema beyond additive optional fields.
- Performance optimization of the existing first-stage pipeline beyond instrumentation.

## Child Bead plan

1. Feature: Embedding prompt-template support — config structs, embed_query/embed_documents split, template application, fingerprint changes.
2. Feature: OpenAI-compatible reranking pipeline — Reranker trait, config, chat client, integration with search pipeline, fallback.
3. Feature: Search pipeline metrics and diagnostics — SearchMetrics/SearchDiagnostics structs, instrumentation, aft_search response enhancement, warning thresholds.
4. Story: TUI/status integration for semantic search diagnostics — status panel additions.
5. Task: Config documentation and examples — README/docs update with example configs.
6. Task: Test suite for semantic search upgrade — unit and integration tests.

## Dependency strategy

Only true blockers use blocking dependencies. Parent-child is containment only. The epic is the parent container; children are ordered by implementation sequence.

## Approval gates

- Embedding changes review: verify defaults remain unset, backward compat intact.
- Reranking integration review: verify config validation, SSRF policy, no API keys in logs.
- Metrics/diagnostics review: verify no raw queries or code snippets in logs.
- Security review for reranker endpoint URL validation matching existing embedding SSRF policy.

## Verification strategy

- `cargo build` — compiles cleanly.
- `cargo test` — all existing + new tests pass.
- Manual test with default fastembed config — behavior unchanged.
- Manual test with openai_compatible mock for prompt templates.
- Manual test with reranker mock for reordering and fallback.
- `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.
- `cargo fmt` — formatting consistent.

## Research routing

Enhancement ideas discovered during this program should go to a backlog bead (future).

## Closure criteria

- [ ] Required child Beads complete.
- [ ] Verification complete.
- [ ] Handoff/summary recorded.

title: TUI/status integration for semantic search diagnostics
description:
## Objective

Extend AFT's TUI/status panel to show semantic search pipeline health. The goal is to surface enough diagnostic information for a user to quickly assess whether semantic search is working correctly — without overwhelming the display. The TUI integration MUST first verify the TUI framework's capabilities (dynamic panels, expand/collapse support) before implementation, because the approach forks based on what the framework supports.

## Current behavior

- AFT TUI displays basic status information (connection, working directory, etc.).
- No semantic search-specific status, diagnostics, or warnings.
- No visibility into index health, embedding backend, or query performance.

## Desired behavior

When semantic search is configured and the TUI supports expandable detail panels:
- Compact one-line summary showing: backend name (truncated to fit), model name, index entry count, last-query latency.
- Expandable detail view showing: index status (ready/building/empty/stale/unavailable), score distribution from last query (min/median/max), rerank status (enabled/disabled, model when enabled, latency when applicable), reranker failure fallback message, low-confidence warnings.
- Color-coded status: green (ready/healthy), yellow (building/degraded), red (unavailable/error), white (empty/disabled) — only if the TUI framework supports colors.

When semantic search is configured but the TUI does NOT support expandable detail panels:
- Two-line compact view: line 1 shows backend + model + chunk count; line 2 shows last query latency + score range + status indicator. No expandable details — all essential info fits in two lines. Color coding used if supported.
- If even two lines would exceed the TUI layout capacity, fall back to a single line with the most critical indicator (status emoji/color) and model name only.

When semantic search is not configured:
- No semantic search panel shown (current behavior).

All status text truncated to fit within the TUI's display boundaries (default max width: 40 chars per field, configurable). Long model/backend names are truncated with ellipsis.

## Scope

In scope:
- Investigate TUI/status component architecture to determine: dynamic panel support, expand/collapse support, color support, update/refresh mechanism.
- Based on TUI capabilities, implement the appropriate visual approach (see desired behavior above).
- Define a polling mechanism: TUI reads from a shared diagnostics snapshot updated by Feature 3 (metrics/diagnostics). Poll interval: 1s (configurable).
- Ensure the status panel updates live as queries execute and diagnostics arrive.
- When semantic search is disabled: no panel shown.
- Model/backend name truncation with ellipsis at configurable max width.

Out of scope:
- Redesign of the entire TUI/layout system.
- Changes to non-semantic-search TUI components.
- Persistent metric storage (handled by Feature 3).
- Documentation (separate bead).

## Pre-condition: TUI framework investigation

BEFORE any implementation work on this bead, complete this discovery:

1. Locate the TUI/status component source code.
2. Determine: does it support conditional/dynamic panels?
   - If YES: implement the single-line + expandable detail approach.
   - If NO: implement the always-visible two-line compact approach (no expandable section).
3. Determine: does the TUI framework support color output?
   - If YES: use color-coded status indicators.
   - If NO: use text-only status labels.
4. Determine: what is the refresh/update cycle? Push-based (events) or pull-based (timer)?
   - Based on this, design the data path from Feature 3's diagnostics snapshot to the TUI display.
5. Document findings and confirm the visual approach before proceeding to implementation.

If the pre-condition reveals that the TUI framework is fundamentally unsuitable for dynamic status panels, this bead must be restructured — consult with the user or epic owner.

## Mandatory code/spec reading before editing

- [ ] TUI/status component source.
- [ ] Feature 3 (metrics/diagnostics) response types to understand what data is available.
- [ ] Spec §5 for TUI/status requirements.

## Implementation plan

1. [Pre-condition] Investigate TUI framework capabilities (see pre-condition section above).
2. Based on findings, create the diagnostics-to-TUI data flow (polling or event-based).
3. Implement status line rendering for the determined approach.
4. Wire up data refresh from Feature 3's diagnostics snapshot.
5. Handle all status states (ready, building, empty, stale, unavailable).
6. Handle disabled/unconfigured state (no panel shown).
7. Add truncation for long model/backend names.
8. Add color coding if supported.
9. Handle reranker status display.
10. Handle reranker failure message.
11. Add tests.
12. Run validation.

## Error handling and edge cases

- Feature 3 diagnostics snapshot temporarily unavailable (e.g., first query not yet run): show "waiting for first query" or similar.
- Long backend names: truncate with ellipsis at configurable max width (default: 40 chars).
- Model name missing at startup: show "initializing..." until backend reports model.
- Index status unknown: show "unknown" rather than incorrect status.
- TUI refresh race: "last query" means "last completed query at poll time" — document that there is a refresh latency.
- State flicker during index rebuild: debounce status display — show stable state only after it persists >500ms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TUI framework investigated and approach confirmed (expandable vs compact) before implementation begins.
- [ ] Status line visible when semantic search is configured.
- [ ] Index status displayed correctly: ready/building/empty/stale/unavailable.
- [ ] Embedding backend name and model name shown (truncated with ellipsis if needed).
- [ ] Index entry count displayed.
- [ ] Last query latency shown (updated on each poll cycle after first query completes).
- [ ] Score min/median/max from last query shown.
- [ ] Rerank status shown: enabled/disabled.
- [ ] Reranker model name shown when reranking is enabled.
- [ ] Rerank latency shown (when applicable).
- [ ] Reranker failure fallback message visible ("rerank failed, using original ordering").
- [ ] Low-confidence warning indicator visible.
- [ ] Color coding applied if TUI supports colors (green/ready, yellow/degraded, red/error, white/empty).
- [ ] No semantic search panel shown when semantic search is not configured.
- [ ] Status updates at configurable polling interval (default: 1s).
- [ ] All existing tests pass unchanged.

## Validation commands

- `cargo build` — compiles.
- `cargo test` — all tests pass.
- `cargo clippy` — no new warnings.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: Feature 3 (metrics/diagnostics) — the TUI consumes diagnostics data.
- Blocks: nothing.
- Strong interface coordination needed with Feature 3: the diagnostics snapshot struct that the TUI polls must be agreed upon before both are implemented.

## Review requirements

- User PR review required.
- Review by someone familiar with the TUI framework.

## Handoff requirements

- Files changed: TUI status component, data pipeline from diagnostics to TUI.
- Validation evidence: test output + pre-condition investigation findings.
- Discovered Beads: if the TUI investigation reveals significant refactoring is needed, a follow-up bead may be required.
- Spec updates if behavior changed: spec is the primary artifact.
